Twelfth Night

A Twelfth Night Celebration at Home

Mark the end of Christmastide with a cozy and traditional Twelfth Night celebration, bringing ancient revelry and delicious feasting right into your home.

  1. Morning

    Kitchen Preparations Begin

    Start baking your King Cake, carefully hiding the bean charm within, and prepare your Figgy Pudding. Get your chosen roasted meat ready for the oven.

    Recipes: Traditional King Cake · Figgy Pudding · Roasted Pork Loin with Apple and Sage

  2. Afternoon

    Warm the Spiced Ale

    Gently heat your spiced ale, allowing its comforting aromas to fill your home, preparing for the evening's toasts and merriment.

    Recipes: Spiced Ale (Wassail)

  3. Late Afternoon

    Dismantle the Greenery

    Gather all your Christmas decorations and greenery. Traditionally, these are taken down on Twelfth Night to ward off bad fortune for the coming year.

  4. Early Evening

    A Toast to Good Fortune

    Raise a cup of warm spiced ale to your household's health and prosperity, embracing the spirit of wassailing from the comfort of your home.

    Recipes: Spiced Ale (Wassail)

  5. Evening

    The Grand Feast

    Gather around the table for a hearty meal of roasted meats, celebrating the abundance of the season before the fasting of Epiphany begins.

    Recipes: Roasted Pork Loin with Apple and Sage

  6. After Dinner

    Crowning the King or Queen

    Serve your King Cake! The lucky person who finds the hidden bean charm is crowned the king or queen of the revels for the night.

    Recipes: Traditional King Cake

  7. Late Evening

    Sweet Endings

    Conclude your festive meal with a rich figgy pudding, a sweet and traditional dessert to mark the end of the Christmastide season.

    Recipes: Figgy Pudding

May your Twelfth Night be filled with warmth, good fortune, and sweet memories as you bid farewell to the festive season.
